01 Listen

Your recording

Source labels stay hidden until you reveal.

Original recordings work best. AASIST provides a one-way safety challenge to human-leaning upload results; it cannot clear a synthetic warning. No account or audio upload to a server.

Speak naturally for 3–15 seconds. Recording stops automatically at 15 seconds.

Microphone off

Microphone permission is requested only when you start. Audio stays on this device. Playback through a speaker can hide synthetic artifacts, so a human-leaning microphone result will return uncertain. Upload the original digital file when possible.

Signal facts

MEASURED LOCALLY

Frequency evidence

LOG-MEL · 20 Hz–8 kHz

Energy across the same 26 mel bands used by the feature model. This view helps inspect silence, bandwidth and repeated structure; it is not proof that audio is synthetic.

Where to listen again

2 s WINDOWS · 1 s HOP

The feature-based detector scans 2-second windows. Scores are exploratory, not calibrated probabilities or proof of an edit.

Next step Verify consequential messages through a known official channel. This tool cannot confirm who spoke or whether a statement is true.

OPERATIONAL SAFEGUARD

Detection becomes a decision protocol

A viral audio clip can trigger fraud, panic or disinformation before its source is checked. A model score is one signal; high-impact messages still require an independent official-channel check.

  1. 01
    Screen

    Review the verdict, uncertainty, detector agreement and signal quality.

  2. 02
    Contain

    Pause redistribution when the result is synthetic, conflicting or uncertain.

  3. 03
    Verify

    Contact the claimed office using a known number, domain or internal directory.

  4. 04
    Record

    Keep the original file and download the assessment for accountable review.

Why this mattersReplay through a speaker can erase useful artifacts. GovVoice Shield therefore treats microphone audio cautiously and recommends the original digital file. It screens audio provenance; it does not decide whether a spoken claim is factually true.
